rotation.name: Recommended mix: Cover crop – sunflower – vetch – sorghum – millet
rotation.description: Cover in both winters with drought-tolerant summer crops.
rule_ids: seleccion:mejor de 3 variantes mixtas con tus prioridades
management: terminate the cover crop in time (August-September) so the soil profile recharges before the summer crop
obtain cover-crop seed and budget for planting and termination costs

advice.text: It is the best-scoring rotation for this scenario and your priorities.
Sunflower: high water-shortage risk in Dec. Check the profile's available water before planting and adjust density and planting date.
From May 2032 to Nov 2032 the field has 7 months without a living crop (1 with bare soil) in the windy season. Consider a cover crop (for example rye or vetch) or leaving the residue standing.
MODIS NDVI: in recent years the field spent ~8 months per year with little vegetation. With this rotation it would be ~3 months without a living crop: less time with exposed soil.

data_used: NASA POWER (DATO DE MUESTRA, 2016-2025): rain, ET0 and days above 35 °C each month.
SMAP L4 (DATO DE MUESTRA): moisture +38 % vs. normal; it adjusts the water risk at the start of the first season.
MODIS NDVI MOD13Q1 (DATO DE MUESTRA): months with little vegetation observed in the field.
assumptions: Seasons from July to June. Planting and harvest dates are typical for each crop.
Heat risk: frequency of days with Tmax > 35 °C times the crop's sensitivity, higher in full growth.
Water risk: uncovered demand from the monthly balance (Kc x ET0, effective rain and profile water).
Residue protects the soil for a few months depending on the previous crop; after that it counts as bare soil.
The seasons repeat the same average weather: it is not a year-by-year forecast.
